title: Chicken and Bacon Pie
subtitle: A creamy double-crust pie of chicken thigh, back bacon, and leek
excerpt: Tender chicken thigh and smoked back bacon in a creamy leek sauce, sealed under a shortcrust lid. A generous, crowd-pleasing pie that reheats well the following day.
sourceNotes: A classic British combination; this version uses a béchamel-style cream sauce rather than a roux-thickened stock for a cleaner flavour.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the assembled unbaked pie. Bake from frozen at 180C for 55 to 60 minutes, covering with foil for the first 30.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The filling can be made up to two days ahead. Keep it covered in the fridge and assemble on baking day.

content.text: This is a deeply savoury, creamy pie that sets well enough to slice at the table. Chicken thighs hold their texture better than breast meat and stay moist in the sauce. The filling must be cold before it goes into the pastry case, or the base will not bake through properly.

items.prepNote: two thirds for the base, one third for the lid

content.text: Melt half the butter in the large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken chunks in batches until golden on all sides. Remove and set aside. Add the bacon strips and cook until lightly coloured. Remove and set aside.
Add the remaining butter to the pan and soften the leeks for 5 minutes. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Gradually pour in the stock, stirring constantly to avoid lumps. Add the cream and mustard and stir until the sauce is smooth and thick.

Return the chicken and bacon to the pan. Add the thyme leaves. Season with salt and black pepper. Simmer gently for 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in the parsley, and spread the filling on a large plate to cool completely.
Heat the oven to 200C. Line a 23cm deep pie dish with two thirds of the pastry, leaving a 2cm overhang. Chill for 30 minutes.

Spoon the cold filling into the case. Brush the overhang with beaten egg. Roll out the remaining pastry for a lid, lay it over the filling, and press the edges together to seal. Trim, crimp, and cut a slit in the top. Glaze with beaten egg.
Bake for 40 to 45 minutes until the pastry is deep gold. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.cause: The stock was added too fast over a high heat.
items.fix: Add the stock in a steady stream while stirring. If lumps form, whisk vigorously over the heat or pass through a sieve before adding the chicken back.

items.symptom: The base pastry is uncooked in the middle.
items.cause: The filling was warm when it went in, or the pie was not baked on a preheated surface.
items.fix: Always cool the filling fully. Place a heavy baking tray in the oven as it heats, then set the pie dish on it to crisp the base from below.

items.symptom: The filling spills over the rim during baking.
items.cause: Too much filling was packed in, or the lid was not sealed tightly.
items.fix: Leave a 1cm gap at the top of the filling and ensure the lid is firmly crimped. Place the pie dish on a baking tray to catch any overflow.
